issue.title: Nested lambdas lead to undefined-variable messages

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
This code:

get = lambda x: lambda y: getattr(x, y)

Results in this warning:

Undefined variable 'x' (undefined-variable)

But there should be no warning since x is defined by the outer lambda.

issue.title: wrong 'undefined-variable' in nested lambda

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
The following `python3` code triggers `pylint` to report `E:  1,34: Undefined variable 'v' (undefined-variable)`.

``` python
fs = map(lambda v: (lambda: print(v)), [1,2,3])
for f in fs:
  f()
```

``` bash
$ python3 -m pylint --version
__main__.py 1.5.5, 
astroid 1.4.5
Python 3.5.1+ (default, Mar 30 2016, 22:46:26) 
[GCC 5.3.1 20160330]
```

issue.title: Spurious error

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
This program:

``` python
F = (lambda b: lambda: b + 7)(3)
print(F())
```

Produces this output:

```
$ python2.7 -m pylint -r n example.py 
No config file found, using default configuration
************* Module example
C:  1, 0: Missing module docstring (missing-docstring)
E:  1,23: Undefined variable 'b' (undefined-variable)

$ python3.5 -m pylint -r n example.py 
No config file found, using default configuration
************* Module example
C:  1, 0: Missing module docstring (missing-docstring)
E:  1,23: Undefined variable 'b' (undefined-variable)
```

Running it raises no errors, however:

```
$ python3.5 example.py 
10

$ python2.7 example.py 
10
```

Is the error spurious?

issue.title: False positive with undefined-variable with regard to lambda lookups in class scope

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
Originally reported by: **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**

---

```
#!python



class C:
    foo = 1
    bar = lambda: C.foo

E:  3,18: Undefined variable 'C' (undefined-variable)


```

Originally reported in #342.

---
- Bitbucket: https://bitbucket.org/logilab/pylint/issue/704

body: It may be unpythonic, but it's a good workaround for this issue: https://stackoverflow.com/a/34021333/5421745.

If there’s someone knowlegdable  about the system who could provide pointers, that might help this issue get resolved sooner.
For example what files to look at,
And any concerns we should keep in mind for issues we might run into while working on the error.

@dbieber The error is emitted here https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/blob/6a0d9d5df29a151a2c76614623acaf492be3746f/pylint/checkers/variables.py#L1278.  As you can see from that function, the scoping lookup is a bit messy in `pylint`, so what I think this fix should do is to change this function to do a proper lookup in the upper scope of that `lambda` for finding this variable.

issue.title: Incorrect report of undefined variable in nested lambdas

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a file with the code:

    func = lambda v: lambda: v+1

2. Check with pylint
3. Receive error:

    Undefined variable 'v' (undefined-variable)

### Current behavior

Pylint incorrectly thinks a lambda inside a lambda does not have access to any of the variables in the parent lambda, and so reports any usage of those variables as missing, when they are not.

### Expected behavior

The above code should not trigger an "undefined-variable" error.

### pylint --version output

    pylint 1.9.2
